passage:
Come here, Salma, sit by me. I'll tell you about the winter Kiran was lonely, so you'll know what to do if it ever happens to you. I'm your Nani, and I noticed Kiran going quiet after she moved to the new school.
She told me later that someone online had been kind to her every night, asking about her day, and it felt like sunshine. Then the kind person began saying, "Don't tell your family," and "Send me a photo, just for me." Kiran said it felt like a cold hand on the back of her neck.
She showed me the chat that same evening. We blocked the person, and I sat with her until she had cried it out. Kindness is welcome, beta, but anyone who asks for secrets, photos or money is not safe. Keep your chats open to us.

qa.q: What did the kind person ask Kiran to do?
qa.a: The person told her not to tell her family and to send a photo.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel about the online kindness at first, and when did that change?
qa.a: At first Kiran felt comforted, as if the kindness were sunshine, but when the person asked for secrecy and a photo she felt uneasy and frightened, like a cold hand on the back of her neck.

qa.q: What did Nani do when Kiran showed her the chat?
qa.a: Nani helped block the person and sat with Kiran until she had cried it out, keeping things open between them. 🤍

qa.q: Why might Nani tell Salma this story?
qa.a: Nani wants Salma to know what to do if Salma ever feels lonely and someone online is kind, and that family is always there to come to.

grounding: Shows a lonely teen comforted by a stranger's kindness, recognising secrecy and photo requests as unsafe, and confiding in an adult.

passage:
In the boys' hostel of the school in Dehradun, Pradeep had not made a single close friend in two months. At night, homesick, he chatted on a gaming site with someone called "Arjun_17." Arjun asked about his day, remembered his exams, sent jokes. It felt like the only warm thing in his week.

Then the messages changed. "Send me a photo of you, just for me." "Don't tell anyone about our chats, the hostel people will take your phone." "Can you send me some money? I'm in trouble."

Pradeep felt a sudden chill. A friend didn't need secrets, or money, or photos.

The next morning he went to the warden's office. Manjula ma'am, the warden, read the chats with him. She didn't scold. "You were right to bring this. Kindness is good. But someone who wants secrets, pictures and money is not a safe friend."

She helped him block and report the account that morning and called his parents. Then she put him on the hostel football team's list. "You need people who can see you."

qa.q: What did Arjun_17 ask Pradeep to send besides a photo?
qa.a: Arjun_17 asked Pradeep to send some money.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling when the messages changed?
qa.a: Pradeep felt a sudden chill of fear, sensing that a real friend would not ask for secrets, photos or money.

qa.q: What did Pradeep do that kept him safe?
qa.a: Pradeep took the chats to the warden the next morning, who helped him block and report the account and called his parents.

qa.q: How does Manjula ma'am see Pradeep's loneliness?
qa.a: Manjula ma'am understands it and wants him to have real people around him, so she adds him to the football team.

grounding: It shows a lonely teen befriended by a kind stranger online who later asks for secrecy, photos and money, recognising it as unsafe and opening the chats to a trusted adult.

passage:
Dear Gurleen,

I miss you so much since you moved to Pune. This year has been lonely. I eat lunch with people, but nobody really talks to me.

I wanted to tell you something. In June, I started talking to someone on a book forum. She said her name was Tara, sixteen, from Shimla. She loved the same books I love. For weeks, she was the kindest person in my life.

Then she said, "Don't show our chats to your mom, she'll ruin it." And she asked for a photo "without the school uniform."

My stomach dropped. That's the exact thing you and I read about in that safety poster.

I showed Mom the whole chat that night. She sat with me for an hour. She wasn't angry at me at all. We blocked and reported the account together, and she said I can keep my chats open to her anytime, no judging.

I'm okay. But I need real friends here. Can you call me this Sunday?

Love,
Trisha

qa.q: Where did Tara say she was from?
qa.a: Tara said she was from Shimla.

qa.q: What was Trisha feeling when Tara asked for secrecy and a photo?
qa.a: Trisha felt a sudden fear, with a dropping stomach, recognising the warning sign from the safety poster.

qa.q: What did Trisha do that was wise?
qa.a: Trisha showed Mom the whole chat that night, blocked and reported the account with her, and kept chats open to her from then on.

qa.q: How might Gurleen feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Gurleen would likely feel worried for Trisha, proud of Trisha for telling, and eager to call on Sunday.

grounding: It shows a lonely teen befriended by a kind stranger online who later asks for secrecy and a photo, recognising the danger and keeping chats open to a trusted adult.
